In September 2005, World of Warcraft's new Zul'Gurub raid gave its boss, Hakkar, a contagious spell called Corrupted Blood, and a bug let hunter and warlock pets carry it out of the dungeon and into the capital cities. Shopkeepers and guards caught it but didn't die, so they kept infecting everyone who walked past, and the BBC reported deaths thought to be in the thousands. Players fled, healers rushed in, and some spread it on purpose. Blizzard's quick fixes didn't hold, it restarted its servers about a week in, and the real fix, a patch that made pets immune, took nearly a month. Blizzard called it just a bug. catalog.title: WoW Forever Just Cut Dungeon Runs in Half
catalog.description:
A recent WoW: Forever hotfix: "Players can now reset and enter each dungeon a maximum of 5 times per hour (was 10)."

That matches the original Classic Era lockout, and Wowhead says it's unclear whether 10 was ever intended. A full clear usually takes 30 minutes or more, so most players won't notice. Runs under 12 minutes will.

Wowhead thinks the target is solo gold farms, where players abuse enemy pathing (players can jump, mobs typically can't), pull the trash and reset. The new Krol'dok Stronghold farm takes about 5 minutes. Blizzard didn't give a reason.

The same hotfix also fixed the Demonic Aegis bonus staying in Demon Armor and Demon Skin after unlearning the talent.
